abstract_sentences.text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are conversational interfaces.

evidence.anchor: LLMs are conversational interfaces

abstract_sentences.text: As such, LLMs have the potential to assist their users not only when they can fully specify the task at hand, but also to help them define, explore, and refine what they need through multi-turn conversational exchange.
abstract_sentences.comparison: fully specified task versus iterative multi-turn refinement
abstract_sentences.transition: extends the opening definition into practical scope

evidence.anchor: help them define, explore, and refine what they need

abstract_sentences.text: Although analysis of LLM conversation logs has confirmed that underspecification occurs frequently in user instructions, LLM evaluation has predominantly focused on the single-turn, fully-specified instruction setting.
abstract_sentences.comparison: real underspecified instructions versus single-turn evaluation

evidence.anchor: evaluation has predominantly focused on the single-turn

abstract_sentences.text: In this work, we perform large-scale simulation experiments to compare LLM performance in single- and multi-turn settings.
abstract_sentences.transition: answers the gap with the study design

evidence.anchor: compare LLM performance in single- and multi-turn settings

abstract_sentences.text: Our experiments confirm that all the top open- and closed-weight LLMs we test exhibit significantly lower performance in multi-turn conversations than single-turn, with an average drop of 39% across six generation tasks.
abstract_sentences.comparison: multi-turn versus single-turn across tested models and tasks

evidence.anchor: average drop of 39% across six generation tasks

abstract_sentences.text: Analysis of 200,000+ simulated conversations decomposes the performance degradation into two components: a minor loss in aptitude and a significant increase in unreliability.
abstract_sentences.transition: turns the headline drop into a decomposition

evidence.anchor: a minor loss in aptitude and a significant increase in unreliability

abstract_sentences.text: We find that LLMs often make assumptions in early turns and prematurely attempt to generate final solutions, on which they overly rely.

evidence.anchor: make assumptions in early turns and prematurely attempt

abstract_sentences.text: In simpler terms, we discover that when LLMs take a wrong turn in a conversation, they get lost and do not recover.
abstract_sentences.transition: compresses the decomposition into the title metaphor

evidence.anchor: they get lost and do not recover

method_summary.formal_objects: Original query q, intended output Y*q, atomic content units I(q), shard sequence q', per-run score S_i, mean P, aptitude A90, unreliability U10-90.
method_summary.input: A fully specified benchmark instruction plus task evaluator.
method_summary.output: A validated shard set and simulated conversations with per-turn answer scores.
method_summary.state: Conversation history, revealed and unrevealed shards, assistant response strategy, extracted answer, and task score.
method_summary.objective: Compare matched task performance under different information-disclosure schedules.
method_summary.assumptions: Shard equivalence preserves intended output; one shard is revealed at most per turn; the LLM user is a behavior probe rather than a user model.
method_summary.first_formalization: P, A, U appear in §4.2 (PDF p.6); q/I(q)/q' appear in Appendix B (PDF p.17).
method_summary.transition_sequence: state_problem → define_component → instantiate_algorithm → explain_mechanism → contrast_alternative → setup_notation → derive → define_component → connect_to_prediction

result_inventory.claim: Every tested model degrades on every main task under SHARDED, with 39% average degradation.
result_inventory.value: P is described as approximately 90 in FULL and 65 in SHARDED; Table 1 aggregates a -39% degradation.
result_inventory.comparison: SHARDED versus FULL across 15 models and six tasks.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Per-instruction mean over 10 simulations, then corpus/task/model aggregation; no inferential interval or formal test reported.
result_inventory.author_interpretation: The matched multi-turn setting exposes capability hidden by fully specified evaluation.
result_inventory.adverse_interpretation: The result is conditional on a synthetic, narrow, analytical English stress test.
result_inventory.author_handling: §8 explicitly limits interpretation to a controlled underspecification stress test.

evidence.anchor: every model sees its performance degrade on every task
controlled underspecification stress test

result_inventory.claim: CONCAT largely preserves FULL performance, supporting information preservation under rephrased shards.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate performance ratio across main tasks/models; no uncertainty interval.
result_inventory.author_interpretation: SHARDED loss is not explained by information loss in the shard wording.
result_inventory.adverse_interpretation: Several smaller models retain only 86-92% under CONCAT, so paraphrase is not neutral for all models.
result_inventory.author_handling: The text names these smaller-model exceptions and attributes them to weaker paraphrase robustness.

evidence.anchor: CONCAT performance averaging 95.1%
smaller models struggle to generalize

result_inventory.claim: Stronger models get lost at a similar relative rate to weaker models.
result_inventory.value: Average degradations for named strong models are 30-40%.
result_inventory.comparison: Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5, GPT-4.1 versus smaller models.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Relative degradation aggregated across six tasks; denominator depends on each model's FULL score.
result_inventory.author_interpretation: Single-turn strength does not prevent multi-turn degradation.
result_inventory.adverse_interpretation: Lower-FULL models have less room for relative degradation.
result_inventory.author_handling: The authors state this denominator effect directly.

evidence.anchor: get equally lost in conversation
less scope for degradation

result_inventory.claim: The average degradation is dominated by unreliability rather than aptitude loss.
result_inventory.value: Aptitude drops 16%; unreliability increases 112%; fixed-instruction best-to-worst runs differ by 50 points on average.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Per-instruction 90th percentile and 90th-minus-10th percentile range, averaged across corpora.
result_inventory.author_interpretation: Lost in Conversation is principally a reliability phenomenon.
result_inventory.adverse_interpretation: With only 10 runs per instruction, empirical tail percentiles are coarse and their estimation uncertainty is not reported.
result_inventory.author_handling: Appendix E explains the estimands, while §9 notes that scaling repetitions could uncover additional findings.

evidence.anchor: average drop of 16%
average increase of 112%
scaling up the experiments further might help

result_inventory.claim: The main effect appears once instructions span two or more turns in the gradual experiment.
result_inventory.value: Both GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini show a large reliability increase from two shards onward.
result_inventory.statistical_method: 10 simulations per instruction/model; 31 claimed source instructions expanded to 248 variants, though Appendix L contains a conflicting 'eight instructions' sentence.
result_inventory.author_interpretation: Providing everything at once is the only tested granularity that restores reliability.
result_inventory.adverse_interpretation: The source instructions all had eight shards and are more complex than the corpus average; the sample-count inconsistency adds reporting ambiguity.
result_inventory.author_handling: §5.3 acknowledges the complexity selection and says a varying-complexity design would confound granularity.

evidence.anchor: with two-shard instructions and beyond
inherently more complex than the corpus average
leading to a total of eight instructions

result_inventory.claim: Later first answer attempts are associated with higher performance on Code and Math.
result_inventory.value: 30.9 for first attempt in the first 20% versus 64.4 in the last 20%.
result_inventory.comparison: Earliest versus latest first-answer timing bins.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Conversations binned by normalized first-answer turn; averages across 15 models on two tasks.
result_inventory.author_interpretation: Premature answer attempts can plant incorrect assumptions.
result_inventory.adverse_interpretation: Timing is observational, and four tasks could not be analyzed because attempts usually occurred on turn one.
result_inventory.author_handling: The appendix reports the two-task restriction and labels the assumption mechanism a hypothesis.

evidence.anchor: score of 30.9, less than half of the 64.4
only two observed a significant range

result_inventory.claim: Answer attempts grow longer over turns and remain longer even when correct.
result_inventory.value: Final SHARDED attempts are 20-300% longer; correct Code is 27% longer and correct Database is 14% longer than FULL.
result_inventory.comparison: Successive SHARDED attempts versus FULL/CONCAT and correct-only subsets.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Mean extracted-answer character length by attempt index; filtered correct subset for Code/Database.
result_inventory.author_interpretation: Models retain invalid assumptions and bloat later solutions.
result_inventory.adverse_interpretation: Length is a proxy; it does not directly identify which tokens encode invalid assumptions.
result_inventory.author_handling: The text calls the result a hint of qualitative worsening, not a direct semantic analysis.

evidence.anchor: tend to be 20-300% longer
hinting that the solutions are qualitatively worse

result_inventory.claim: Summary citations overweight first and last turns relative to middle turns.
result_inventory.value: At turn 8, 20% cite turn-8 documents versus 8% for turns 2 and 3.
result_inventory.comparison: Document introduction turn within eight-turn summaries.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Citation shares averaged across 15 models; row totals may be under 100% due to hallucinated citations.
result_inventory.author_interpretation: Loss-in-the-middle also occurs across conversation turns.
result_inventory.adverse_interpretation: Model-specific heterogeneity is omitted and the analysis covers only Summary.
result_inventory.author_handling: The authors state the model-specific magnitude varies and defer that analysis.

evidence.anchor: 20% of citations are to documents introduced in turn 8
do not include model-specific analyses

result_inventory.claim: More verbose conversations perform worse on five of six tasks.
result_inventory.value: Average P is 40.7 in the shortest quintile and 35.6 in the longest; task-level gains for short responses are described as 10-50%.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Ten runs split into five bins of two for each model-instruction pair, then averaged by task.
result_inventory.author_interpretation: Short responses avoid unnecessary assumptions and keep the conversation focused.
result_inventory.adverse_interpretation: Actions reverses the pattern; verbosity may be an outcome of difficulty rather than a cause.
result_inventory.author_handling: The Actions exception is reported, and the causal explanation is marked as a hypothesis.

evidence.anchor: On five of the six tasks
We hypothesize that deterioration due to over-verbosity

result_inventory.claim: RECAP and SNOWBALL help but do not restore FULL/CONCAT performance.
result_inventory.value: SNOWBALL mitigates 15-20% of the FULL-to-SHARDED deterioration; RECAP performs better but is operationally unrealistic.

final_judgment.single_storyline: 把同一 fully-specified instruction 拆成逐轮揭示的 shards，在任务与 evaluator 不变的配对设计中观察 performance；结果显示主损失来自 run-to-run unreliability，而非单纯 aptitude 下降，并以 premature attempts、answer bloat 与 turn-position attention 作为描述性机制线索（PDF p.2 §1，anchor: 'same information'; p.8 §5.2，anchor: 'increased model unreliability'）。
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: 正文保留 sharded simulation 的核心流程、六任务与 15 模型规模、P/A/U 定义、Table 1、Figure 5、gradual sharding、stakeholder implications 与外部效度限制，因此读者可在正文判断主效应与描述性分解（PDF p.4 §3.3，anchor: 'five types of conversation'; p.7-p.9 §5）。
final_judgment.appendix_moves: 附录承载 shard 的形式化性质与生成流程、simulator inspection、四项行为分析、所有 mitigation/temperature/translation 结果、task evaluator 细节、model versions、failure case 与完整 prompts。迁移不妨碍判断 39% 主效应，但削弱了正文对所谓 root causes 的自足性（PDF p.8 §5.2，anchor: 'Appendix F explores potential root causes'; p.21-p.25 Appendix F）。
final_judgment.best_pattern: 最有效模式是 matched FULL/CONCAT/SHARDED control 与 P/A/U decomposition 配合：CONCAT 排除大部分 rephrasing/information-loss 解释，Figure 5 再把均值下降拆成 aptitude 与 unreliability（PDF p.4 §3.3，anchor: 'control to ensure'; p.8 §5.2，anchor: 'average increase of 112%'）。
final_judgment.largest_gap: 最大缺口是机制主张的识别强度：Appendix F 主要给 correlation、length proxy 与 attention distribution，且覆盖任务不一；结论却将 premature assumptions 与 over-reliance 写成现象构成。另有 gradual sample 与 simulator inspection 两处 denominator 冲突（PDF p.22-p.25 Appendix F；p.34 Appendix L；p.19-p.20 Appendix D）。
final_judgment.transfer_rule: 未来论文若主张 interaction-induced degradation，应对同一底层任务做 matched disclosure comparison，加入等信息 paraphrase control，先报告 per-unit stochastic distribution，再将最关键 mechanism test 留在正文，而非只放 appendix（PDF p.4 §3.3；p.6 §4.2；p.8 §5.2）。
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: 该规则适用于能定义同一 target output、能构造 information-preserving disclosure schedules、并可重复评分的交互任务；不应直接外推到 creative、multimodal、non-English、real-user 或 episodic append-only tasks（PDF p.11 §8，anchor: 'focus on analytical tasks'; p.28 §G.3，anchor: 'task is episodic'）。

evidence_coverage.counting_note: Counts structured records with non-empty page evidence; the not_applicable component-deletion placeholder is excluded. Final-judgment strings carry inline page citations and are not added to this count.
